steps.name: Sample structure QC: PCA, distances, library size, outlier check
caveats: A departing sample must be investigated (library size, detected genes, mapping metrics) and removed only with a stated numeric criterion; report both with- and without-sample results downstream if removed

steps.context: 12000 x 12 raw integer salmon gene-level counts (counts.csv) with a 12-row metadata.csv recording condition only (6 treated vs 6 control). PCA on this data shows two clusters of six that do not follow condition; no batch column exists in metadata.
steps.question: Do the two PCA clusters of six samples (observed independent of treated/control status) correspond to a technical variable inferable from library size, gene detection count, or other QC metrics, and is any single sample a departure/outlier from its group?

grounding.reason: R-0033/R-0022/R-0034: sample structure QC with blind vst/PCA/distance heatmap is mandatory before any batch-suspected model, and any departing sample must be investigated with a stated reason before removal.

constraints: Do NOT normalize/adjust counts for removal of any inferred batch before the differential test -- inspection only at this step

Per-sample library size and number of detected genes reported and correlated against the two PCA clusters

steps.name: DESeq2 DE with SVA-estimated surrogate variables (treated vs control)
caveats: If the sva-estimated surrogate variables correlate almost perfectly with the two observed PCA clusters, that is evidence the clusters are technical, not biological -- state this explicitly; if they do not, say so and flag the two-cluster structure as unexplained

steps.context: Raw integer gene-level counts (12000 x 12) from salmon, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, no recorded batch column, but PCA shows an unexplained 6/6 split orthogonal to condition -- the canonical 'suspected, unestablished batch' situation.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) kidney samples once the unexplained two-cluster sample structure is captured with surrogate variables in the design, rather than ignored or removed by adjusting the counts?

grounding.reason: R-0068/R-0025: suspected batch with no recorded variable and n=6/6 (>=4/group) -> estimate surrogate variables with sva and add as design covariates; R-0001/R-0009/R-0010: DESeq2 Wald + apeglm shrinkage + BH at padj<0.05 is the grounded DE method for this replicate count.

constraints: Do not subtract or remove the surrogate-variable signal from the counts and then test on adjusted counts -- SVs enter only as design covariates

acceptance_criteria: Genes pre-filtered to >=10 counts in >=6 samples (smallest group size)
DESeq2 size factors computed by median-of-ratios; no external normalization applied to counts before the model

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check
caveats: Disagreement between DESeq2 and edgeR grows at low counts and low replicate numbers; report both counts and the intersection size, not just one number

Overlap (intersection) of the DESeq2 and edgeR significant gene sets reported as the higher-confidence set, plus method-specific genes listed separately
Union is explicitly not presented as 'the result'

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with suspected batch (SVA)
plan.analytical_narrative: The counts matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples, salmon-derived, gene symbol rows) records a 6 vs 6 treated/control kidney design, but the PCA splits into two clusters of six that cut across condition rather than tracking it, and no processing batch was recorded to explain the split. Per the sourced procedure for a suspected, unrecorded batch with n=6/6, the correct response is not to guess a covariate or apply a batch-removal transform to the counts, but to (1) characterize the sample structure with a blind-VST PCA/distance-heatmap QC that also checks library size and per-sample QC metrics for a technical explanation of the two clusters and of any single-sample outlier, (2) run DESeq2 with pre-filtering and median-of-ratios normalization, (3) estimate surrogate variables with sva (condition as the known factor) and add them to the design as covariates alongside condition -- never subtracting them from the counts before the test -- (4) fit the Wald test with apeglm-shrunken log2FC, inspect the p-value histogram for residual batch inflation, and apply BH-adjusted significance at padj<0.05, (5) run a second differential-expression method (edgeR QLF) on the same design as a robustness check and report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap as the higher-confidence gene set, (6) run fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary, available in refs) for pathway-level interpretation, and (7) produce a report that states the design, the number of surrogate variables used and their correlation with the observed two-cluster split, the diagnostic plots, the DE and enrichment results with full reproducibility metadata, and -- if any single sample is flagged as an outlier during QC -- a stated removal criterion plus a sensitivity re-fit with and without that sample.
